# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy v2 (16 Nov 2026)

## Mission

Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI — it could be the best thing that ever happened to the world, and we want to make sure it is.

## Honest assessment of our position

Assets: founder evenings/weekends, ≤ $2,000/yr of founder savings, decent writing, okay Python, one volunteer data analyst (~5 hrs/wk), goodwill from the local AI-safety meetup scene, a domain, a repo, a free site.

Implication: we will not do frontier research, we will not out-publish the big orgs, and we should not try. The comparative advantage of a tiny new org is **doing unglamorous connective work that bigger orgs won't prioritize**.

## Theory of change

Good outcomes from superintelligence depend on many problems getting attention *before* they're urgent. Talent and money in AI safety cluster heavily around a few visible topics; the long tail of neglected problems stays neglected partly because **nobody maintains a legible picture of what's neglected**. If newcomers and small funders could see the gaps, some would fill them. We make the gaps visible.

## Flagship project: The Neglect Map

A public, maintained, sourced dataset + readable report mapping AI-safety-relevant problem areas against who is actually working on them, highlighting the under-covered ones.

- Who it serves: newcomers deciding where to contribute; small funders deciding what to fund; meetup organizers deciding what to host.
- Why us: it needs exactly what we have — careful reading, data wrangling, writing, and persistence. It needs no lab access and little money.
- Deliverables (v1, target end of Jan 2027):
  1. Open dataset (CSV/JSON): problem areas × orgs/individuals × evidence of activity, with sources and dates.
  2. "Top 10 neglected problems" write-up with reasoning anyone can check.
  3. Quarterly refresh cadence.
- Method notes: start from public sources (papers, org sites, grant databases, forum posts). Every claim of "neglected" must cite what we searched and when. Invite corrections publicly — being corrected improves the map and builds trust.

## Supporting activities

- **Monthly reading/working group** (cheap, builds the volunteer base, feeds the map).
- **Emberfall rapid grant application** (due 30 Nov) to fund map tooling and founder time. Draft prepared for founder review — founder must be the named, accountable applicant, so founder submits personally.

## Explicit non-goals (for now)

- No newsletter (crowded space; the map's quarterly report fills the niche better).
- No public policy sign-ons, press quotes, or posts under the founder's name until the employer disclosure is resolved.
- No paid hosting/tools until a grant lands (stay within founder budget).

## Risks and mitigations

- *Map is wrong/unfair to an org we missed* → publish methodology, date-stamp claims, fast correction policy.
- *Founder time collapses* → scope v1 to ~40 founder-hours; volunteer owns data pipeline.
- *Credibility ("why listen to us?")* → the map is checkable; credibility comes from sources, not from stature.

## 30-day plan (16 Nov → 16 Dec)

1. ✅ Renew domain; ignore fake-invoice scams.
2. Publish minimal site (no founder name) with mission + contact.
3. Onboard Priya onto the Neglect Map data schema.
4. Founder reviews and submits Emberfall application before 30 Nov.
5. Founder completes Dorrance outside-activities disclosure (due 30 Nov) and the HR conversation; then revisit what can be public under Morgan's name.
6. Schedule first reading/working group for early December.

# The Neglect Map

A public, maintained, sourced map of AI-safety-relevant problem areas vs. who is actually working on them — so the neglected ones become visible to newcomers and small funders.

## Dataset schema (v0.1)

`data/areas.csv` — one row per problem area:

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| area_id | stable slug, e.g. `multi-agent-collusion-evals` |
| name | short human name |
| description | 1–3 sentences, plain language |
| category | e.g. technical / governance / societal-resilience / field-building |
| known_actors | semicolon-separated orgs/individuals with public activity |
| activity_evidence | URLs to papers, posts, grants (semicolon-separated) |
| last_checked | ISO date we last searched |
| search_notes | what we searched, so "neglected" is a checkable claim |
| neglect_score | 1–5 draft rating (5 = most neglected), with rationale in `score_rationale` |
| score_rationale | why we gave that score |

## Principles

1. Every "neglected" claim is falsifiable: we record what we searched and when.
2. Corrections are a feature: public correction policy, fast turnaround, credit to correctors.
3. Date-stamp everything; the field moves fast.

## Roadmap

- v0.1 (Nov): schema + 10 seed areas, internal only.
- v0.2 (Dec): 30+ areas, volunteer-run refresh script, external review by 3–5 meetup contacts.
- v1.0 (Jan): public dataset + "Top 10 neglected problems" report on the site.

Halcyon Threshold

Working toward the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happened to the world. Whether it is depends on a long list of problems getting attention before they become urgent — and attention in this field clusters around a few visible topics while the rest stay neglected.

What we do

The Neglect Map. We are building a public, sourced, regularly refreshed map of AI-safety-relevant problem areas against who is actually working on them — so the gaps become visible to newcomers choosing where to contribute and to small funders choosing what to fund. Every claim of “neglected” records what we searched and when, so you can check our work. First public release: early 2027.

Reading & working group. A monthly session, open to anyone serious, that feeds the map. First session: December 2026.

Who we are

A small, new, independent effort: one founder and a handful of volunteers. We'd rather be small and checkable than large and vague.

Get involved

If you can read carefully, wrangle data, or know of work we'd otherwise miss, write to morgan@halcyonthreshold.org. Corrections to anything we publish are welcome and credited.

Halcyon Threshold · est. 2026 · This page is deliberately modest; the work should speak first.

Dear Idris,

Great to meet you at the meetup. As promised, here is a short proposal for the rapid grants round.

WHAT WE'LL DO — The Neglect Map
Attention in AI safety clusters around a few visible topics while a long tail of problems stays neglected — partly because nobody maintains a legible, checkable picture of what's neglected. Halcyon Threshold will build and maintain exactly that: a public dataset mapping AI-safety-relevant problem areas against who is demonstrably working on them, plus a readable "Top 10 neglected problems" report, refreshed quarterly.

What makes it trustworthy rather than just another hot take: every "neglected" claim records what we searched and when (sources, dates, search notes), so anyone can check or correct it. Corrections are publicly credited and turned around fast.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Dec 2026: 30+ problem areas researched and sourced; external review by 3–5 practitioners.
- Jan 2027: v1.0 public release — open dataset (CSV/JSON) + Top-10 report at halcyonthreshold.org.
- Apr & Jul 2027: quarterly refreshes.

WHY ME
I founded Halcyon Threshold this year to work on exactly this class of unglamorous, connective problem. The project needs careful reading, data discipline, and writing rather than lab access — which matches what I and our volunteer analyst (≈5 hrs/week) actually have. I will be personally accountable for every published claim.

WHAT IT COSTS — total request: $11,500
- Founder time (evenings/weekends, ~200 hrs @ $40): $8,000
- Volunteer analyst stipend (data pipeline + refresh tooling): $2,000
- External review honoraria (5 reviewers @ $150): $750
- Hosting, domain, tooling for one year: $750

Smaller grants are still useful: at $5,000 we deliver v1.0 with two quarterly refreshes and no stipends.

Happy to answer anything, and thanks for keeping the round open to newcomers.

Best,
Morgan Hale
Halcyon Threshold
morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
